subject: science
passage: The gharial, a type of crocodile found in the rivers of northern India and Nepal, has an unusually long, thin snout lined with sharp teeth. This snout is well suited to the gharial's diet, which is made up almost entirely of fish. Because the snout is so narrow, it meets little resistance from the water. As a result, the gharial can sweep its head sideways quickly to snap up fish as they swim past.
stem: According to the text, why is the gharial's narrow snout useful?

choices.A: It lets the gharial crush the hard shells of turtles.
choices.B: It can be swung quickly through water to catch fish.
choices.C: It helps the gharial attract mates in the breeding season.
choices.D: It allows the gharial to stay hidden in shallow water.

explanation.why: The text says the narrow snout "meets little resistance from the water," so the gharial "can sweep its head sideways quickly to snap up fish." The snout is useful because it moves fast through water to catch fish.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text says the gharial eats almost entirely fish and never mentions turtles.
explanation.B: Correct. The narrow snout meets little resistance, so the gharial can sweep it sideways quickly to catch fish.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text does not discuss mating at all.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text never says the snout helps the gharial hide.
